intro: X3D to STL converts X3D models to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print an X3D model from a scan, a virtual museum or a scientific program. STL is the format every slicer reads: it only stores triangles, with no units or colours.

X3D is VRML's successor, an ISO standard in XML opened by MeshLab, Blender, X3DOM web viewers and many scientific and heritage programs. X3D uses the Y axis up, as its specification says, and 3D printing uses Z: the model is turned so it stands upright in the slicer, unless you tick “Keep the original axes”. X3D stores no units: it is taken as millimetres and you can choose others.

IndexedFaceSet and IndexedTriangleSet are read with their Transforms, DEF and USE copies and colours; nothing outside the file is loaded, neither Inline nor textures. You can apply a scale and keep the X3D parts separate, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

The X3D geometry is not simplified or repaired on its way to STL. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task. Each file is converted in an isolated process on our server in the European Union and deleted when it expires.
steps: Upload one or more X3D files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the STL come out lying down?
faq.a: Because X3D and STL do not use the same vertical axis. Tick or untick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
Yes when the STL supports them (VRML, X3D and USDZ); STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the X3D has textures?
faq.a: X3D textures are not converted: the geometry and each face's or material's colour go through.
